cues.en: So, as we've seen, collaborative filtering can produce great results that have been shown to work really well in real, large-scale situations.
cues.zh: 如前所見，協同過濾能產生很好的結果，也證明能在真實大型情境中有效運作。

cues.en: So, why should we look for something that's even better?
cues.zh: 那為什麼還要尋找更好的方法？

cues.en: Collaborative filtering has been criticized as having limited scalability, since computing similarity matrices on very large sets of items or users can take a lot of computing horsepower.
cues.zh: 有人批評協同過濾的擴展性有限，因為對大量項目或使用者，計算相似度矩陣，需要很強的運算能力。

cues.en: I don't really buy this, however.
cues.zh: 不過，我不太認同。

cues.en: As we've seen, using item-based collaborative filtering reduces the complexity of that substantially, to the point where you can compute an entire similarity matrix for extremely large product catalogs
cues.zh: 如前所見，項目式協同過濾能大幅降低複雜度，甚至能在單一機器上，為極大商品目錄，計算完整的相似度矩陣。

cues.en: on a single machine.
cues.zh: 只用一台機器就行。

cues.en: And even if you couldn't, technologies such as Apache Spark allow you to distribute the construction of this matrix across a cluster if you need to.
cues.zh: 即使不行，必要時 Apache Spark 等技術，也能把矩陣建立工作分散到叢集。

cues.en: A legitimate problem with collaborative filtering, though, is that it's sensitive to noisy data and sparse data.
cues.zh: 不過，協同過濾確實有一個問題：對雜訊與稀疏資料很敏感。

cues.en: You'll only get really good results if you have a large data set to work with that's nice and clean.
cues.zh: 只有資料集夠大，而且乾淨，才會有真正好的結果。

cues.en: So, let's explore some other ways to make recommendations.
cues.zh: 因此，探索一些其他推薦方法。

cues.en: We'll group these together under the label, model-based methods, since instead of trying to find items or users that are similar to each other, we'll instead apply data science and machine learning techniques
cues.zh: 把它們統稱為模型式方法，因為不再找彼此相似的項目或使用者，而是應用資料科學與機器學習技術，

cues.en: to extract predictions from our ratings data.
cues.zh: 從評分資料擷取預測。

cues.en: Machine learning is all about training models to make predictions, so we'll treat the problem of making recommendations the same way.
cues.zh: 機器學習就是訓練模型來預測，因此也用相同方式看待推薦問題。

cues.en: We will train models with our user ratings data and use those models to predict the ratings of new items by our users.
cues.zh: 用使用者評分資料訓練模型，再用模型預測使用者對新項目的評分。

cues.en: This puts us squarely in the space of the rating prediction architecture that SurpriseLib is built around, and although we've shown it's not always the most efficient approach,
cues.zh: 這讓我們完全進入 SurpriseLib 所採用的評分預測架構。雖然已經證明它不一定最有效率，

cues.en: it allows us to repurpose machine learning algorithms to build recommender systems, some of which are very good at predicting ratings.
cues.zh: 但能讓我們把機器學習演算法轉用於推薦系統，其中有些很擅長預測評分。

cues.en: Whether they make for good top-N recommendations is something we'll need to find out.
cues.zh: 至於是否能產生好的 Top-N 推薦，還需要找答案。

cues.en: There are a wide variety of techniques that fall under the category of matrix factorization.
cues.zh: 有很多技術屬於矩陣分解這個類別。

cues.en: These algorithms can get a little bit creepy.
cues.zh: 這些演算法甚至會有點讓人毛骨悚然。

cues.en: They manage to find broader features of users and items on their own, like action movies or romantic.
cues.zh: 它們能自行找出使用者與項目的廣泛特徵，例如動作片或浪漫程度。

cues.en: Although the math doesn't know what to call them, they are just described by matrices that describe whatever attributes fall out of the data.
cues.zh: 雖然數學不知道該如何命名，只會用矩陣描述從資料浮現的各種屬性。

cues.en: The general idea is to describe users and movies as combinations of different amounts of each feature.
cues.zh: 一般概念是，把使用者與電影，描述成不同份量的各種特徵的組合。

cues.en: For example, maybe Bob is defined as being 80% an action fan and 20% a comedy fan.
cues.zh: 例如，Bob 可能被定義為 80% 動作片迷、20% 喜劇片迷。

cues.en: We'd then know to match him up with movies that are a blend of about 80% action and 20% comedy.
cues.zh: 那麼就知道，應該匹配大約 80% 動作、20% 喜劇的電影。

cues.en: That's the general idea, let's dig into how it works.
cues.zh: 這是大致概念，深入看看如何運作。

cues.en: Working backwards from what we want to achieve is usually a good approach, so what are we trying to do when predicting ratings for users?
cues.zh: 從目標倒推，通常是好方法。預測使用者評分時，究竟想做什麼？

cues.en: Well, you can think of it as a filling in a really sparse matrix.
cues.zh: 可以把它想成填滿一個非常稀疏的矩陣。

cues.en: We can think of all our ratings as existing in a 2D matrix, with rows representing users and columns representing items, in our case, movies.
cues.zh: 把所有評分視為二維矩陣，列代表使用者，欄代表項目，在這裡是電影。

cues.en: The problem is most of the cells in this matrix are unknown.
cues.zh: 問題是，矩陣大部分儲存格未知。

cues.en: Our challenge is to fill those unknown cells in with predictions.
cues.zh: 挑戰是，用預測填滿未知儲存格。

cues.en: Well, if we're trying to come up with a matrix at the end of the day, maybe there are some machine learning techniques that work on matrices we can look at.
cues.zh: 既然最後想產生矩陣，也許可以看看有哪些處理矩陣的機器學習技術。

cues.en: One such technique is called principal component analysis, or PCA.
cues.zh: 其中一種叫做主成分分析，簡稱 PCA。

cues.en: Principal component analysis is usually described as a dimensionality reduction problem.
cues.zh: 主成分分析，通常被描述為降維問題。

cues.en: That is, we want to take data that exists in many dimensions, like all of the movies a user might rate, into a smaller set of dimensions that can accurately describe a movie, such as its genres.
cues.zh: 也就是，把存在於多維空間的資料，例如使用者可能評分的所有電影，轉成較少、卻能準確描述電影的維度，例如類型。

cues.en: So, why is there a picture of a flower on the screen?
cues.zh: 那為什麼畫面上有花？

cues.en: Well, it's a little hard to imagine how this works on movies at first, but there's a data set on iris flowers that makes for a good example of PCA in action.
cues.zh: 一開始不容易想像這如何用在電影，但鳶尾花資料集，是展示 PCA 運作的好例子。

cues.en: Look closely at an iris, and you'll see that it has a bunch of large petals on the outside and some smaller petals on the inside.
cues.zh: 仔細看鳶尾花，外側有一些大花瓣，內側有較小花瓣。

cues.en: Those inner petals aren't called petals at all, they're called sepals.
cues.zh: 那些內側的部分其實不叫花瓣，而叫花萼。

cues.en: So, one way to describe the shape of a specific iris flower is by the length and width of its petals, and the length and width of its sepals.
cues.zh: 因此，描述某朵鳶尾花形狀的一種方式，是花瓣的長寬，以及花萼的長寬。

cues.en: So, if we look at the data we're working with in the iris data set, we have length and width of petals and sepals for each iris we've measured.
cues.zh: 看看鳶尾花資料集，每朵測量過的花，都有花瓣與花萼的長度、寬度。

cues.en: So, that's a total of four dimensions of data.
cues.zh: 總共是四維資料。

cues.en: Our feeble human brains can't picture a plot of 4D data, so let's just think about the petal length and width at first.
cues.zh: 我們脆弱的人腦，無法想像四維資料圖，所以先只看花瓣長度與寬度。

cues.en: That's plotted here for all of the irises in our data set.
cues.zh: 這裡畫出資料集中所有鳶尾花。

cues.en: Without getting into the mathematical details of how it works, those black arrows are what's called the eigenvectors of this data.
cues.zh: 不深入數學細節，黑色箭頭是所謂資料的特徵向量。

cues.en: Basically, it's the vector that can best describe the variance in the data and the vector orthogonal to it.
cues.zh: 基本上，就是最能描述資料變異的向量，以及與它正交的向量。

cues.en: Together, they can define a new vector space, or basis, that better fits the data.
cues.zh: 兩者能一起定義一個更符合資料的新向量空間，也就是基底。

cues.en: These eigenvectors are our principal components of the data.
cues.zh: 這些特徵向量，就是資料的主成分。

cues.en: That's why it's called principal component analysis.
cues.zh: 所以叫做主成分分析。

cues.en: What we are trying to find are these principal components that describe our data, which are given by these eigenvectors.
cues.zh: 我們試圖找出描述資料的主成分，而它們由這些特徵向量給出。

cues.en: Let's think about why these principal components are useful.
cues.zh: 想想為什麼主成分有用。

cues.en: First of all, we can just look at the variance of the data from that eigenvector.
cues.zh: 首先，可以只看資料相對於該特徵向量的變異。

cues.en: That distance from the eigenvector is a single number, a single dimension that is pretty good at reconstructing the two-dimensional data we started with for petal length and petal width.
cues.zh: 離特徵向量的距離，是單一數字、單一維度，卻很能重建原本花瓣長寬的二維資料。

cues.en: So, you can see how identifying these principal components can let us represent data using fewer dimensions than we started with.
cues.zh: 因此可以看到，識別主成分，就能用比原本更少的維度表示資料。

cues.en: Also, these eigenvectors have a way of finding interesting features that are inherent in the data.
cues.zh: 而且，這些特徵向量，能找出資料內在有趣的特徵。

cues.en: In this case, we're basically discovering that the overall size of an iris' petals are what's important for classifying which species of iris it is, and the ratio of width to length
cues.zh: 這個例子中，基本上發現，鳶尾花花瓣的整體大小，才是分類物種的重要因素，而寬長比

cues.en: is more or less constant.
cues.zh: 大致固定。

cues.en: So, the distance along this eigenvector is basically measuring the bigness of the flower.
cues.zh: 因此，沿著這個特徵向量的距離，基本上衡量花有多大。

cues.en: The math has no idea what bigness means, but it found the vector that defines some hidden feature in the data that seems to be important in describing it, and it happens to correspond to what we call bigness.
cues.zh: 數學不知道「大小」是什麼意思，卻找出一個向量，定義資料中似乎很重要的隱藏特徵，而它剛好對應到我們所說的大小。

cues.en: So, we can also think of PCA as a feature extraction tool.
cues.zh: 所以，也能把 PCA 當作特徵擷取工具。

cues.en: We call the features it discovers latent features.
cues.zh: 它發現的特徵，稱為潛在特徵。

cues.en: So, here's what the final result of PCA looks like on our complete four-dimensional iris data set.
cues.zh: 這就是對完整四維鳶尾花資料集做 PCA 的最後結果。

cues.en: We've used PCA to identify the two dimensions within that 4D space that best represents the data, and plotted it in those two dimensions.
cues.zh: 使用 PCA，在四維空間中找出最能代表資料的兩個維度，再把資料畫在這兩維上。

cues.en: PCA by itself will give you back as many dimensions as you started with, but you can choose to discard the dimensions that contain the least amount of information.
cues.zh: PCA 本身會傳回與原本相同的維度數，但你可以選擇捨棄資訊量最少的維度。

cues.en: So, by discarding the two dimensions from PCA that told us the least about our data, we could go from four dimensions down to two.
cues.zh: 因此，捨棄 PCA 中最少描述資料資訊的兩維，就能從四維降成二維。

cues.en: We can't really say what these two dimensions represent.
cues.zh: 無法真正說明這兩維代表什麼。

cues.en: What does the X axis in this plot mean?
cues.zh: 這張圖的 X 軸代表什麼？

cues.en: What does the Y axis mean?
cues.zh: Y 軸又代表什麼？

cues.en: All we know for sure is that they represent some sort of latent factors, or features, that PCA extracted from the data.
cues.zh: 唯一確定的是，它們代表 PCA 從資料擷取的某種潛在因子或特徵。

cues.en: They mean something, but only by examining the data can we attempt to put some sort of human label on them.
cues.zh: 它們有某種意義，但只有檢視資料，才能試著貼上人類理解的標籤。
